place: Hansel Valley, western Box Elder County, Utah

defining_record.label: Compute Atlas data-center listing "Stratos AI Data Center Campus" (JODY data-center entity)

summary: A data center campus proposed for ranch land in Hansel Valley, in western Box Elder County.

In October 2026, Bar H Ranch, Inc. asked the Utah Division of Water Rights to move water now used to irrigate the ranch to the project. The filing names O'Leary Digital Utah DC Sub I, LLC as the developer.
The state has not decided the filing, and it has been protested.
summary_sources: Utah Division of Water Rights: Change Details for a55167

latest.title: Change application a55167 filed on water right 13-2
latest.body: Bar H Ranch, Inc. asks to change where, how and for what the water of right 13-2 is used: up to 1,712 acre-feet a year (4 cubic feet per second) from Salt Wells Spring Stream, moving from ranch irrigation to power generation and data-center uses. The Division lists it as Unapproved and Protested.
latest.changes_status: Does not change the project's lifecycle. It is an application, not an approval.
source: Change Details for a55167 (Division of Water Rights)
latest.observed: JODY first saw this filing on the state's pending list on Oct 28, 2026.

next.text: The Division's record shows no hearing and no State Engineer decision on a55167. It is marked Protested.
next.scope: No upcoming official hearing or deadline has been confirmed in the sources we track.

impacts.text: Up to 1,712 acre-feet a year from Salt Wells Spring Stream. The applicant says the project would consume no more than 1,009 acre-feet, against 1,009 to 1,291.6 acre-feet consumed by irrigation today.
impacts.who: Applicant's statement in the state filing

impacts.text: The filing lists a power use: "Wonder Valley Power ... Steam Generation Power Plant, Rated at 7500 MW".
A study reported by Utah News Dispatch and KSL projects health effects from the project's emissions. The developer's team disputes it.
impacts.who: Reported by news outlets, not verified by JODY
